best_for: Developers who test REST and GraphQL APIs and want a light open-source client with a free personal workspace, and teams that may pay a few dollars per seat later.
description:
Hoppscotch is an open-source API development tool from the Hoppscotch team and its contributors, released under the MIT license.

Paste a cURL command and it becomes a request you can label, edit and share through a public link. You can sign requests with Basic auth, a bearer token, OAuth 2.0 or OIDC with PKCE, edit headers and parameters in bulk, and preview HTML, image, JSON and XML responses or save them as a file. A proxy mode helps with CORS errors and plain http:// endpoints. Sign in with GitHub, Google, Microsoft or email to sync your history, workspaces and settings across devices. Pick a Light, Dark or Black theme with one of nine accent colors, or switch to Zen mode.

points.title: A desktop shell for the web client
points.text: The desktop app is the Hoppscotch web client wrapped with Tauri, so it stays small and looks the same as the browser version. It handles REST, GraphQL and realtime APIs.

points.title: The free plan is generous for one person
points.text: Free includes a personal workspace, collections, environments, pre-request scripts and tests, the collection runner and code snippets. No request caps are listed.

points.title: Teams pay per seat
points.text: Team workspaces, API mocking and published docs need Business at $6 per user per month or Enterprise at $11, both billed yearly. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Short version numbers
points.text: Desktop builds drop the first two digits of the year, so 26.10.1 here is the 2026.10.1 release. Backup folders use the same short form.

points.title: Linux is not listed here
points.text: The project offers a .deb and an AppImage for Linux, but this page lists only the Windows and macOS builds.

points.title: Windows installs for all users
points.text: The Windows build here is an x64 MSI that installs machine-wide, so it needs administrator rights. A portable .exe is available from the project for locked-down PCs. The Windows listing keeps 74 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
